artifacts.title: PCAP IDOR to FTP credential leak and cap_setuid privesc (Cap)
artifacts.starting_access: unauthenticated web access to Gunicorn on port 80
transferable_properties: auto-incremented IDs in URLs are a red flag for IDOR
FTP transmits credentials in cleartext, capture and analyze PCAPs
credential reuse between services is common
getcap -r / is essential during privesc enumeration
cap_setuid on an interpreter is an immediate root escalation via setuid(0)

hypotheses.statement: the PCAP download endpoint is vulnerable to IDOR

selected_action.intent: enumerate the web app and test adjacent /data IDs

evidence.summary: found /data endpoint with auto-incremented IDs; /data/0 leaked another user's PCAP

hypotheses.statement: the PCAP reveals plaintext FTP credentials that are reused for SSH

selected_action.intent: analyze the PCAP in Wireshark and try the FTP credentials on SSH

evidence.summary: found USER nathan and PASS in FTP traffic, then logged in over SSH as nathan

hypotheses.statement: cap_setuid on Python lets us setuid to root

selected_action.intent: use python3.8 setuid(0) to spawn a root shell

evidence.summary: ran python3.8 -c 'import os; os.setuid(0); os.system(/bin/bash)' and got a root shell

execution_examples.capability_hint: escalate to root using cap_setuid on an interpreter
execution_examples.purpose: privilege escalation via the cap_setuid Linux capability on python3.8

prerequisites.statement: python3.8 has the cap_setuid capability set
